source_uses.fact: Planning controls address hazardous-substance consent and development around hazardous establishments
Hazardous substances consent is required at defined thresholds and HSE is a statutory consultee on applications
HSE Planning Advice Web App considers consultation zones plus development type, size and intensity
HSE land-use planning methodology uses inner, middle and outer consultation zones and sensitivity levels
HSE is a statutory consultee for relevant planning applications within consultation distances around major hazard sites and pipelines
COMAH 2015 framework covers establishments with dangerous substances and provides public establishment information
COMAH aims to prevent and mitigate major accidents affecting people and the environment
Public COMAH service supports establishment searches and describes controls for operational establishments above regulatory thresholds
Current HSE COMAH pages provide location-search access to establishments in an area
COMAH enforcement is by the competent authority, jointly involving Environment Agency and HSE or ONR as applicable; page updated 24 April 2026
The London Plan 2021 remains the current adopted planning framework while the next plan is prepared
Historic London hazardous-substances policy illustrates the established principle of site-specific HSE methodology and consultation; it is retained only as historical context, not current policy

examples: A COMAH establishment search hit requires exact spatial relation to its consultation distance before affecting a candidate
Presence of hazardous-substance consent does not mean every nearby parcel is automatically unsuitable
HSE inner/middle/outer zones must be evaluated with the proposed development sensitivity level
A pipeline or installation consultation distance is not a generic radius that can be invented without HSE data
No HSE search result cannot be claimed unless the official location query was actually executed for the parcel
Historic London Plan hazardous policy is context only and is not the current adopted policy source
COMAH operator controls reduce accident likelihood but do not remove planning consultation requirements
No promotion without exact parcel geometry plus current HSE/COMAH location and consultation evidence where relevant
